hints: Look at the axes: the vertical axis is extension in cm and the horizontal axis is force in kN, so read the force that gives 4.0 cm extension.
Recall that elastic potential energy equals the work done to stretch the spring, which is the triangular area under a force against extension graph.
Convert the 4.0 cm to metres and the 30 kN to newtons before evaluating $\frac{1}{2}Fx$ to get joules.
walkthrough: Read the graph at extension $4.0 \text{ cm}$ on the vertical axis. The straight line reaches $30 \text{ kN}$ on the force axis, so $x = 4.0 \text{ cm}$ and $F = 30 \text{ kN}$.
Convert to SI units for energy in joules: $x = 4.0 \text{ cm} = 0.040 \text{ m}$ and $F = 30 \text{ kN} = 30000 \text{ N}$.
State the rule for a spring obeying Hooke's law: elastic potential energy is the area of the triangle under the force-extension graph, $E = \frac{1}{2}Fx$.
Substitute values with units: $E = \frac{1}{2} \times 30000 \text{ N} \times 0.040 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the intermediate product $30000 \times 0.040 = 1200$, then halve it to get $E = 600 \text{ J}$, with unit $\text{N m} = \text{J}$. This is option C
